title: Review of c11's active-nematic colony (SIMD): nucleation, rods and binary fission replicate on fresh seed 31 (24 persistent splits, generation 4, merge/split 0.29); motion stays under 3 body lengths (max 2.9)
summary: Fresh seed 31, labkit T=1000. From uniform phi plus white noise, faint nuclei appear by t=40, about five acquire order by t=85 and stretch into rods carrying a vortex pair by t=135; rods grow and split by elongation and a central pinch, and the colony spreads until rods fill most of the domain by t~700, as in the claim (rerun/seed31/sheet.png). labkit: 42 splits, 24 persistent, max generation 4, 12 merges (ratio 0.29), 7 nucleations. 48 long-lived tracks move >= 1 body length but the best is 2.9 body lengths (motion_seed31.txt), below the 3-body-length line for M; the claim's seeds reach 3.5-5.7. I support S, I and D; M is not seen on my seed.

observations.S: rerun/seed31/sheet.png t=0: white noise on a uniform phi; nuclei at t=40, rods at t=135
observations.I: rerun/seed31/sheet.png t=135-1000: rods of a regulated length (~12 px) that stay separate between fissions
observations.D: rerun/seed31/lineage.png: 24 persistent splits, max generation 4, merges 12 (ratio 0.29); central-pinch fissions visible t=135-480

seeds_run.result: pass for S, I, D; motion max 2.9 body lengths

verdicts.limitation: M is short on my seed: the longest net path is 2.9 body lengths in t=1000, and the author notes speed is not dt-converged (dt/2 doubles it), so M rests on the claim's seeds (3.5-5.7) only. The colony grows on an imposed chemostat supply. I did not run the zeta=0 twin or dt/2. Only ~5 of many early nuclei become rods; the rest dissolve.
